Poirot gathered us in the drawing-room, and for a moment he simply looked at each face in turn, as if he were reading a page. “Mesdames, messieurs,” he said, “I ask your pardon for the trouble. But a small thing does not fit, and I cannot sleep when something does not fit.” Nobody spoke. The clock on the mantel ticked. “The coffee,” he went on, “was taken to the study at nine. By whom? And who, afterward, entered the room?” A glance passed between the housekeeper and the secretary; it was brief, but he saw it. He smiled gently, and waited, and the silence in the room grew heavier than before.
